title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 43-45): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'schéma spatial', a combinatorial model of space. It is a set A of 'figures' carrying a sub-figure relation ⊴, a support map |·|, and a primitive relation ≪ (with an 'interior' variant ≪̊). It is called 'spatial' because ≪ should be describable through ⊴ and |·| alone, i.e. through the 'space occupied' by a figure. On p.43 he asks when a weaker structure (A, ⊴, |·|) comes from a spatial schema (A, ⊴, ≪̊, |·|). From (A, ⊴, |·|) he builds an ordered set Σ of 'regions' with a complementation structure 𝒞 (written ∁), which lets |·| be defined on Σ, and a map Dép: A → Figel^ord(Σ) into the 'ordered elementary figures' of Σ.

This page defines those elementary figures. They are families 𝔖 of elements of Σ satisfying two conditions:
(a) every S in 𝔖 is non-empty (S ≠ ∅_Σ);
(b) distinct members are mutually exclusive: S ≠ T implies S ≤ ∁T or T ≤ ∁S.
In modern terms, they are families of pairwise disjoint non-zero elements of an ortho-/Boolean-like poset. They presumably carry an order (the 'ord' superscript).

On Figel(Σ) there is already a relation ≪̊. Pulling it back gives X ≪̊ Y :⇔ Dép(X) ≪̊ Dép(Y), which is a preorder on A. The first condition is that this preorder be an order. That is condition (ii): Dép is injective (Dép X = Dép Y ⇒ X = Y). The result is a structure (A, ⊴, ≪̊, |·|) satisfying Ax 1 a), b), c).

He then wants the derived relation ≪ to coincide with the relation induced from ≪ on Figel(Σ), i.e. Dép should reflect ≪. He starts the proof ('Supposons Dép(X) ≪ Dép(Y), donc...'). On p.45 he completes it by factoring through an elementary sub-figure 𝔏 = Dép(Y') with Y' ◁ Y, and then checks Ax 2-4.

So the page is a step in a representation theorem: characterize those abstract figure structures that embed into the canonical structure of elementary figures over a 'space' Σ with complementation.
errors: Condition (ii) is necessary for ≪̊ to be antisymmetric only if one also assumes Dép(X) ≪̊ Dép(Y) and Dép(Y) ≪̊ Dép(X) imply Dép X = Dép Y, i.e. that ≪̊ on Figel(Σ) is itself antisymmetric. This is implicit and not stated.
The final argument ('Supposons Dép(X) ≪ Dép(Y) donc') is left incomplete on this page. It continues on p.45.

ideas.what: Elementary figures of Σ as families of non-empty, pairwise exclusive (S ≤ ∁T) elements of an ordered set with complement
ideas.modern_name: antichains of pairwise disjoint nonzero elements / orthogonal families in an orthoposet (cf. partitions in Boolean algebras, mereotopology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Boolean algebra / orthomodular poset theory); in mereotopology Whitehead, Tarski, Clarke

ideas.what: Transport of a relation along a map Dép and requiring injectivity so that the pulled-back preorder is an order
Representation problem: when does an abstract structure (A, ⊴, |·|) arise from a 'spatial schema', i.e. embed into the canonical structure of elementary figures of a region-poset with complement
ideas.modern_name: representation theorems for region-based / point-free geometries (mereotopology, contact algebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Laguna, Whitehead, Tarski; contact algebras: Dimov–Vakarelov, Düntsch–Winter (1990s-2000s)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to themes alluded to in Récoltes et Semailles about 'géométrie tempérée'/combinatorial foundations of space, but not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'schémas spatiaux' (figures, sub-figures, supports, a primitive 'interior/precedence' relation ≪, and a representation via region-posets with complement) is an unpublished point-free/region-based geometry program. It parallels the later mereotopology and contact-algebra representation theorems, a connection apparently never drawn.
missed.quote: La première condition, c'est que cette relation soit une relation d'ordre, i.e. (ii) Soient X, Y ∈ 𝒜, tels que Dép X = Dép Y, alors X = Y.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: Grothendieck working on axiomatic foundations of spatial reasoning in parallel with region-based theories of space. Mathematically, this page is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step (definition of disjoint families, injectivity condition) inside a little-known unpublished axiomatic program on combinatorial 'spatial schemas'. The program itself is mildly interesting historically, but this page contains no notable result.
transcription_corrections: 'At 1 a) b) c)' should read 'Ax 1 a) b) c)' (axioms, as on p.45).
'Fils(Σ)' is most likely 'Figel(Σ)' (Figel^ord(Σ), elementary figures of Σ), with scribbled corrections.
The marginal header '(d'ensembles ... → Ψ ...)' is probably '(d'ensembles 2 à 2 ...)' (pairwise disjoint sets), with a struck-out word. The 'Ψ' reading is doubtful.
The first line probably reads '[qui] soient compatibles avec les relations d'exclusion' rather than 'doivent compatibles avec les relations'.
The set of figures is 𝒜 (script A), consistent with A on p.43; 𝔖 denotes a family of elements of Σ.
